mission_01: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is the most widely used linear dimensionality reduction technique. It finds orthogonal directions (principal components) that capture maximum variance in the data. The first component captures the most variance, the second captures the second most (orthogonal to the first), and so on. PCA requires data standardization before application, as features with larger scales would dominate the variance. The explained_variance_ratio_ attribute shows how much variance each component captures. PCA is essential for visualization, noise reduction, and preprocessing for downstream models.
mission_02: t-SNE (t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) is a non-linear dimensionality reduction technique optimized for visualization. Unlike PCA, t-SNE preserves local structure, meaning points that are close in high-dimensional space remain close in the embedding. It uses a Student t-distribution to model similarities in the low-dimensional space, which helps separate clusters. t-SNE has two key hyperparameters: perplexity (balance between local and global structure) and learning rate. It is stochastic, so results vary between runs. t-SNE is the go-to technique for visualizing high-dimensional clusters.
mission_03: UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is a modern dimensionality reduction technique that combines the strengths of t-SNE and PCA. Like t-SNE, it preserves local structure, but it also better preserves global structure. UMAP is faster than t-SNE and scales better to large datasets. It has two key hyperparameters: n_neighbors (balance between local and global structure) and min_dist (minimum distance between points in the embedding). UMAP supports both visualization and general dimensionality reduction for preprocessing.
mission_04: Variance threshold feature selection removes features with low variance, based on the assumption that low-variance features provide little discriminatory power. sklearn's VarianceThreshold removes features whose variance falls below a specified threshold. This is a simple, unsupervised feature selection method that does not consider the target variable. It is useful as a preprocessing step to remove constant or near-constant features before applying more sophisticated selection methods. However, it may remove informative features that happen to have low variance.
mission_05: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) is a supervised dimensionality reduction technique that finds linear combinations of features that best separate classes. Unlike PCA, which maximizes variance, LDA maximizes class separability. LDA can produce at most n_classes - 1 components. It assumes features are normally distributed within each class and share the same covariance matrix. LDA is effective when class separation is the primary goal and the assumptions hold. It is widely used in pattern recognition and as a preprocessing step for classification.
mission_06: PCA component analysis involves examining the explained variance ratio, cumulative variance, and component loadings to understand how PCA transforms your data. The explained_variance_ratio_ shows the proportion of total variance captured by each component. The cumulative sum helps determine how many components are needed to retain a desired percentage of variance (e.g., 95%). Component loadings (components_) reveal which original features contribute most to each principal component, providing interpretability for the transformed features.
mission_07: Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) is a wrapper-based feature selection method that recursively removes the least important features. It trains a model, ranks features by importance, removes the least important, and repeats until the desired number of features remains. RFE is more computationally expensive than filter methods but often produces better feature subsets because it considers feature interactions through the model. The support_ attribute indicates which features are selected, and ranking_ shows the elimination order.
mission_08: Comparing dimensionality reduction techniques reveals their complementary strengths. PCA is fast, deterministic, and preserves global variance but may miss non-linear structure. t-SNE excels at revealing clusters but is slow, stochastic, and does not preserve global structure. UMAP balances speed, local structure preservation, and global structure, making it a versatile choice. Understanding these trade-offs helps you select the right technique for your specific use case: PCA for preprocessing, t-SNE for cluster visualization, UMAP for general-purpose reduction.
mission_09: Mutual information feature selection measures the dependency between each feature and the target variable, capturing both linear and non-linear relationships. Unlike correlation-based methods, mutual information detects any statistical dependency. sklearn's SelectKBest with mutual_info_classif selects the top k features with the highest mutual information scores. This filter method is fast, does not require model training, and works well as a first-pass feature selection. It is particularly effective when features have non-linear relationships with the target.
mission_10: A complete dimensionality reduction pipeline chains multiple techniques: standardization, feature selection, and PCA. Standardization ensures features are on comparable scales. Feature selection removes irrelevant or redundant features. PCA further reduces dimensionality while preserving variance. This pipeline approach combines the strengths of each technique: filter methods for speed, wrapper methods for quality, and transformation methods for compactness. Building such pipelines is essential for production machine learning systems where computational efficiency and model performance must be balanced.
